title: Semio Tree TikZ Mechanism
description: Rewrite print/tex/semio-tree.sty as a native TikZ mechanism for rendering phylogenetic/hierarchical trees, mirroring the architecture of semio-graph.sty and semio-table.sty (Figure-window wrapper, kind registry, expl3 primitives, style vocabulary). Originally built on a longtable substrate for pagination, but a table row cannot draw its own connector reliably (row height unknown until the cell breaks), so it was rebuilt on TikZ anchors instead: connectors are drawn via `parent.south west |- child`, which makes connectedness structural. Made the hierarchy depth and geometry parametric (indent step, per-kind depth/font/leading registered via \SemioTreeKind) so a caller can add tree levels beyond the default root/group/leaf without editing the package, verified with working 4- and 6-level test trees. Fixed text-to-connector alignment (branch lands on the first line's cap-height, not floating above it), made header boxes expand to a shared right edge instead of auto-sizing to content, and corrected header-box border weight to match the house-wide 0.75pt hairline standard used by every other table/window border in the system (was borrowed from semio-graph.sty's node-emphasis vocabulary at 1.5-2.25pt). No goal in repo://goals covers report/print tooling under mit-bestand specifically (all listed goals are semio-software-platform scoped); associated with the closest available root goal at the user's explicit instruction rather than leaving this untracked.
summary: Rebuilt print/tex/semio-tree.sty from a longtable-based mechanism to a native TikZ mechanism for phylogenetic trees, matching semio-graph.sty's architecture (Figure-window wrapper via \begin{Figure}, expl3 kind registry, style vocabulary, diagnostics). Connectors are drawn via real anchors (parent.south west |- child), which makes connectedness structural instead of tuned — verified by extracting the compiled PDF's vector paths and confirming zero gaps. Geometry (x = depth * indent step, per-kind font/leading/inlet) is now parametric via \SemioTreeKind, so a caller can add hierarchy levels beyond the default root/group/leaf without touching the package; verified with working 4-level and 6-level test trees (all box levels share one right edge, connectors chain correctly through every level). Also fixed: branch-to-text vertical alignment (was floating above the first line, now lands on its cap-height center, calibrated against real measured output); header boxes now expand to a shared right edge flush with the window instead of auto-sizing to content; header-box border weight corrected from a borrowed graph-diagram emphasis weight (1.5-2.25pt) to the house-wide 0.75pt hairline standard used by every other table/window border in the system. Verified throughout via Tectonic compiles with zero errors/overfull-warnings on the canonical case, plus geometry cross-checked against the pre-existing reference PDF (huerden_final.pdf) with matching step sizes. Not done: the file is not yet committed (working-tree change only); Task #13 (renaming the pre-existing Anhang H so "Hürden der Wiederverwendung" is free for this new appendix) is separate and still pending; the report content itself (the 9-clade taxonomy data) has not yet been re-emitted through this new mechanism.
